result.markdown:
Short answer: **yes, GEO “works” — but not in the way most people think, and it’s not a magic switch.**

“GEO” here usually means **Generative Engine Optimization**: trying to get your content or brand **mentioned or cited inside AI answers** (like ChatGPT-style search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) rather than just ranking on Google results pages. [geo-score.online](https://geo-score.online/learn/what-is-geo?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### So does it actually work in practice?

**Yes, but only conditionally:**

GEO tends to “work” when:
- Your content is **clear, factual, and easy for AI systems to quote**
- You already have some level of **authority or external mentions**
- Your information is **structured (FAQs, definitions, lists, schema, etc.)**
- Other sources also reinforce your claims (AI systems prefer consensus)

It often *doesn’t “work”* when:
- You’re trying to game it with tricks or keyword stuffing
- Your site has **no reputation, backlinks, or citations anywhere**
- Your content is vague, opinion-heavy, or hard to extract cleanly
- You expect predictable rankings (AI outputs are probabilistic)

### The important catch
GEO isn’t a separate “engine you optimize for” in the way SEO is for Google.

AI systems don’t have a single ranking list. They:
- Pull from multiple sources
- Summarize probabilistically
- Change outputs depending on wording, time, and context

That means **you can’t reliably “rank #1 in AI answers” the way you can on Google.**

Research even shows visibility in generative engines is **variable and requires repeated measurement rather than a fixed position**. [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07585?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### The honest takeaway
- GEO is real as a **strategy label**
- The underlying mechanics are real (AI citation + retrieval systems)
- But it’s **not a separate growth channel with guaranteed control**
- It’s closer to: *“good SEO + strong brand presence + structured content + being widely referenced”*

### A useful way to think about it
If SEO is:
> “Can I rank on Google?”

Then GEO is:
> “Would an AI confidently reuse or cite my content in an answer?”

Those overlap a lot—but GEO is **less controllable, more indirect, and harder to measure cleanly.**
